CNN: Trump is changing his policy toward Iran

Yesterday I wrote here ☝️about President Trump's announcement that there are no contacts with Iran—that this is a statement different from what the president has conveyed until now.

According to CNN, the president has decided to change the policy toward Iran and to stop pursuing a quick agreement with Iran.

The emerging new policy: economic, financial, and military pressure until the Iranians decide to become more flexible and reach an agreement that fits President Trump's demands.

##
In my view, such an approach is good for Israel.
Long-term economic strangulation.
The Americans are managing to help transport millions of barrels of oil a day through Hormuz (8–9 million according to the American administration)—and Iran exports nothing.

Saudi Arabia also supports this approach—it fears an American–Israeli military move against Iranian oil infrastructure because it would be the first to pay the price—its energy facilities would be attacked.

There are authentic indications that the Iranians are struggling with the economic pressure—(the American Secretary of the Treasury promised that this week additional significant crippling sanctions would be announced)—the pressure on the Iranian regime is increasing—even domestically.

The big question is: At some point, as a result of the mounting economic pressure, will the Iranians not turn to a preemptive strike in an attempt to break the stranglehold?

We will wait and see.

A few hours later, the UAE announced the cessation of all trade and financial transactions with Iran, until further notice.

This is a painful blow from Iran’s perspective. The UAE has been an economic lifeline for Iran—Iranian nationals have conducted extensive financial activity in the UAE, including in the world of crypto (digital currencies), in order to circumvent the tough economic sanctions against Iran.

This may also be one of the reasons that, amid the wave of Iranian attacks in recent weeks, the UAE was almost off-limits.

##

But you already know the Iranians—they shoot and deny.
